claims.claim: FlashInfer commit 7f614b8 implements the displayed Gated DeltaNet recurrence with independent decay and sigmoid update gates, a delta correction against the decayed-state retrieval, output from the updated state, and a recurrent state whose decode shape has no prior-token axis.

evidence.observation: The reference forms g=exp(-exp(A_log)*softplus(a+dt_bias)) and beta=sigmoid(b), decays state, reads with k, applies beta*(v-read) as an outer-product correction, and computes output from the new state. Decode state is [B,H,V,K] with no context-length axis.

challenge.alternative: The rule is additive-only, retrieves before decay, emits from the old state, or rereads all prior tokens during decode.
challenge.check: Trace the reference operation order and input shapes, including the signs in the expanded remove/write expression.
challenge.outcome: The subtraction, decay-first ordering, updated-state output, and fixed recurrent-state input reject each alternative; K*V work remains, so only context-length independence is claimed.

claims.claim: Pinned Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct has 48 layers arranged as twelve repetitions of three GDN layers and one full Gated Attention layer, 16 QK and 32 value GDN heads of dimension 128, 512 experts with 10 routed plus one shared, 80B total/3B active parameters, and native context 262144.

evidence.locator: num_hidden_layers, full_attention_interval, linear-attention heads, expert fields, and max_position_embeddings
evidence.observation: The immutable config records 48 layers, full attention every fourth layer, 16/32/128 GDN geometry, 512 experts, 10 routed experts, one shared expert, and 262144 positions.
The official card states 80B total and 3B activated parameters and writes the hybrid stack as 12 repetitions of three Gated DeltaNet blocks plus one Gated Attention block.

challenge.alternative: The 3:1 pattern describes heads rather than layers, 512 includes active experts, or fixed GDN state removes cache growth for the full model.
challenge.check: Compare the explicit layer interval, expert-selection fields, and presence of full-attention layers in the immutable config.
challenge.outcome: The interval yields 36 GDN and 12 full-attention layers, active experts are 10 routed plus one shared, and the full-attention quarter retains a context-dependent cache.

claims.claim: Qwen attributes attention-sink and massive-activation mitigation to an output gate in its full Gated Attention path and describes the effect as helpful, not as a required part of the GDN recurrence.

evidence.observation: The official article places output gating in Gated Attention and says it helps eliminate attention sinks and massive activations; it does not make that gate part of the GDN kernel contract.

challenge.alternative: The article proves that output gating is necessary and belongs inside every GDN state update.
challenge.check: Read the named architectural subsection and distinguish Gated Attention from Gated DeltaNet.
challenge.outcome: The source uses a qualified benefit statement for the separate full-attention path, supporting the page's narrower wording.

claims.claim: MLSys 2026 Track C defines distinct decode and variable-length prefill contracts at TP=4 with Q/K/V heads 4/4/8, head size 128, BF16 Q/K/V and output, FP32 state [B or N,8,128,128], the listed gate inputs, and cu_seqlens only for prefill; the derived state sizes are 64 KiB per value head and 512 KiB across eight heads.

evidence.observation: The organizer names Gated Delta Net as Track C and links separate decode and prefill definitions.
Decode fixes q/k/v heads 4/4/8 and d128, uses BF16 token tensors, FP32 [B,8,128,128] state and four gate-related inputs, and returns BF16 [B,1,8,128] plus updated state.
Prefill uses total_seq_len, num_seqs, cu_seqlens[N+1], the same head geometry/dtypes, FP32 [N,8,128,128] state, BF16 token output, and one final state per sequence.

challenge.alternative: qk4/v8 are flattened dimensions, prefill is fixed-length, or 512 KiB applies to each head.
challenge.check: Read the exact axis names and tensor ranks, then recompute 128*128*4 bytes and multiply by eight value heads.
challenge.outcome: The definitions name head counts and variable-length metadata; arithmetic gives 64 KiB per head and 512 KiB across all eight, exactly as scoped.

claims.claim: At commit 7f614b8 FlashInfer provides the cited GDN trace contracts and a prefill dispatcher for SM90 and SM100/SM103, with the latter implemented in CuTe DSL and requiring CUDA 13 or newer and head size 128.

claims.claim: vLLM merge e1d85e5c supports uniform-batch full CUDA-graph capture for compatible recurrent-attention decode, while NVIDIA scopes CUDA-graph benefit to reduced CPU launch overhead rather than a universal workload speedup.

evidence.observation: The backend declares uniform-batch support and implements decode-only full CUDA-graph capture.
NVIDIA explains that setup can dominate short kernels and graph replay reduces CPU launch costs.

challenge.alternative: Graphs remove GPU compute time or guarantee acceleration for every batch shape.
challenge.check: Compare NVIDIA's overhead scope with vLLM's uniform-decode capture conditions.
challenge.outcome: The sources support launch-cost reduction under compatible capture conditions, so the page correctly retains a workload-dependent boundary.

claims.claim: TFLA v3 and its official pinned code apply a second level of sequence parallelism to mLSTM for arbitrarily large chunks, but do not establish a Gated DeltaNet implementation or inline WGMMA/tcgen05 path.

evidence.observation: The official repository describes TFLA for mLSTM, arbitrary large chunks, and PyTorch/JAX/Triton implementations. A pinned-tree search finds no GatedDeltaNet, wgmma, tcgen05, inline PTX, or asm implementation.

challenge.alternative: A general linear-recurrence paper title or Hopper support is sufficient evidence of GDN-specific assembly.
challenge.check: Inspect the published application and search the immutable implementation tree for GDN and instruction-family identifiers.
challenge.outcome: The method and code are mLSTM-scoped and the claimed GDN/assembly identifiers are absent, supporting the explicit boundary.

claims.claim: The page accurately separates GDN's linear sequence scaling from Qwen's implementation-dependent 10x whole-model comparison, and correctly warns that GDN is a learned architectural layer rather than a weight-compatible runtime replacement for softmax attention.

evidence.observation: Qwen reports 10x whole-model inference throughput over Qwen3-32B for contexts above 32K and separately warns that efficiency depends strongly on implementation; it supplies no isolated GDN-kernel GPU result.
The layer owns learned projections, decay/update gates, convolution, output gating/norm, and recurrent state distinct from softmax attention.

challenge.alternative: O(n) complexity alone proves a 10x kernel speedup at 32K, or a serving runtime can swap GDN into arbitrary attention weights.
challenge.check: Inspect the comparison's scope and implementation caveat, then compare GDN's learned parameter/state contract.
challenge.outcome: The result is whole-model and implementation-dependent, and the layer requires GDN-specific learned components; neither alternative is supported.
